attrs.label: Links that editors choose to give you
attrs.html:
Links that editors choose to give you

The links worth having are the ones you can’t buy: an editor on a site your customers read decides your page is useful and links to it. That’s the only kind we build. It’s often called white-hat link building. It takes more effort than buying links, but it’s safe, it lasts, and it sends real visitors your way.

What we do

Links that last for years

  • Personal outreach and digital PR

    Every pitch is researched and written for one editor, journalist or writer.

  • Real sites with real readers

    We check traffic, audience and relevance before we reach out to anyone.

  • Content worth linking to

    Guides, data and tools that give editors a reason to link.

  • Links placed in context

    Inside the article, where an editor chose to put it.

  • Every link reported

    The site, the page, the anchor text and whether it’s still live.

The result: links that keep sending visitors and keep helping you rank.

What we never do

Shortcuts that put your site at risk

  • Buy links or pay for placements

    Paid links break Google’s rules and can get a site penalised.

  • Private blog networks or link farms

    Networks of thin sites built only to pass links.

  • Automated outreach or link software

    No bulk emails, no scraped lists, no bots.

  • Forum, profile or directory spam

    Links nobody reads, which Google ignores or counts against you.

  • Exact-match anchor stuffing

    Unnatural anchor text is one of the easiest patterns for Google to spot.

The risk: links Google ignores, or a penalty that takes months to undo.

attrs.label: Backlink services that earn real links
attrs.html:
Backlink services that earn real links

Six ways we earn links from sites your customers already read. Every link is placed by an editor, not bought.

  • Editorial outreach

    Personal emails to editors and writers who already cover your topic, offering something genuinely useful for their readers.

  • Digital PR and expert quotes

    We answer journalist requests with quotes from your team, earning links from news and industry sites.

  • Guest contributions

    Articles written with your experts for respected industry sites, with a link in the body or author bio.

  • Broken link building

    We find dead links on relevant sites and offer your content as the replacement.

  • Unlinked mentions

    Sites that already mention your brand without linking. We ask them to add the link.

  • Local and industry links

    Associations, partners, suppliers, events and local organisations that should list you.

attrs.label: What does a high-quality backlink look like?
attrs.html:
What does a high-quality backlink look like?

Quality link building isn’t about volume. One contextual, editorial link from a relevant site can do more than a hundred from sites nobody reads. These are the five things we check for every link.

  1. 1

    A relevant site

    The site covers your topic and has an audience your customers belong to.

  2. 2

    Real readers

    People actually visit and read it. Traffic matters more than any authority score.

  3. 3

    In the content

    The link sits inside the article, where an editor chose to place it, not in a footer or a list of links.

  4. 4

    Natural anchor text

    The words that carry the link describe the page they point to, not an exact-match keyword.

  5. 5

    Followed and indexed

    Google can see and count the link, and the page it’s on is indexed.

attrs.label: Do backlinks still matter in the age of AI search?
attrs.html:
Do backlinks still matter in the age of AI search?

Yes. ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google’s AI Overviews build their answers from sources they trust, and links from respected sites are still one of the clearest ways to earn that trust. What has changed is that quality matters more than volume.

The article that links to our client is cited in Google’s AI Overview, and so is the client’s own checklist.

  • AI answers come from pages that rank

    Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode build their answers from its search results, and links still help pages earn those spots.

  • AI tools learn who to trust from the web

    When respected sites in your industry link to you and mention you, AI tools are more likely to know your brand and recommend it.

  • Links bring visitors on their own

    A link in a well-read article sends readers straight to you, however people search.

  • Quality matters more than ever

    AI search makes weak, bought links even less useful. A few links from sites your customers read do the most work.

items.question: What is a link building service?
items.answer: A link building service earns links to your website from other relevant websites, through outreach, digital PR and content. Those links help search engines trust your pages and rank them higher.

items.question: How much do link building services cost?
items.answer: It depends on your market, your goals and how competitive your searches are. We quote every link building package after a free call, with no long contracts.

items.question: How many links do I need each month?
items.answer: Fewer than most people think. A handful of relevant, editorial links each month usually beats dozens of weak ones. We set a pace based on the gap between you and your competitors.

items.question: Do backlinks still matter in the age of AI search?
items.answer: Yes. AI search tools build their answers from sources they trust, and links from respected sites are still one of the clearest signals of trust, for Google and for AI tools. Quality now matters more than volume.

items.question: What is the difference between white-hat and black-hat link building?
items.answer: White-hat link building earns links that editors choose to give. Black-hat link building buys or fakes them with networks, link farms or spam, which breaks Google’s rules and can get a site penalised.

items.question: Do you buy links or use PBNs?
items.answer: No. We never buy links, use private blog networks or link farms, or automate outreach. Every link is earned and reported.

items.question: How long does link building take to work?
items.answer: Most sites see movement within three to six months, depending on competition and how strong the rest of the site is. Links keep working long after they’re earned.

items.question: What is off-page SEO?
items.answer: Off-page SEO is everything outside your website that helps it rank: mainly links, but also brand mentions, reviews and digital PR. Link building is the biggest part of it.

items.question: Do you offer white-label link building for agencies?
items.answer: Yes. We deliver link building under your brand, with white-label reports. See our white-label SEO service.
